source.title: Bias of Stochastic Gradient Descent or the Architecture: Disentangling the Effects of Overparameterization of Neural Networks

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies network width and depth and measures test accuracy, finding different generalization trends for the two ways of increasing overparameterization. It does not test the interpolation-threshold double-descent curve itself, so this is a refinement of scope rather than a direct reproduction.
record.gate_note: The paper reports width and depth sweeps with test accuracy as the outcome. The tested networks are described as overparameterized; the sweeps do not locate or cross the just-fit interpolation threshold. Figures 3 and 4 also plot test accuracy against training-set size, but the text does not report a result that more data raises test error near an interpolation threshold. Figure 12 concerns epoch-dependent loss/accuracy comparisons, not a reported fall-rise-fall test-error trajectory.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps width and depth of networks that all reach zero training error and reports test accuracy. This bears on V1's claim that error keeps falling as size grows past the interpolation point. It never crosses or locates the threshold, so only the post-threshold part of V1 is tested. It shows that part holds for SGD width scaling, not for random interpolators, and not for depth.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the width benefit for SGD comes from its implicit bias, since G&C does not improve. They find depth detrimental in the low-sample regime for both SGD and G&C, showing classical overfitting, which they attribute to architectural bias. They say depth is not claimed to be detrimental in general.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares SGD-trained and randomly sampled zero-training-error networks across width and depth, using test accuracy and margin-related measures; it does not reproduce the original double-descent measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The result differs between increasing width and increasing depth, and between SGD and G&C. The paper also reports that SGD outcomes depend strongly on initialization; suboptimal Uniform [-1, 1] initialization makes SGD perform worse than Kaiming initialization.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The experiments focus on binary classification in a low-sample regime and describe the tested networks as overparameterized, without locating the interpolation threshold. Several reported accuracy trends are qualitative summaries of figures rather than numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported test-accuracy results were omitted.

untested.parts: The first descent and the peak at the just-fit size. Every network tested already interpolates its training set, so no sweep crosses the threshold.
All; Fig 12 shows loss/accuracy by epoch but no fall-rise-fall test error.
All; accuracy-vs-sample-size curves are shown, but no result that more data hurts near a threshold.
All; only neural networks are studied.
All; no label noise or regularization sweeps.
All; the normalization comparison concerns margins, not effective parameter counts.

missing.what: Width and depth trends rechecked at 128 training samples for MNIST 0 vs 7: SGD improves with width; with depth SGD stagnates and G&C worsens.
missing.locator: Appendix D Fig 22; Appendix E Fig 25

record.verdict_notes: All networks, even the narrowest (1/6*, 269 params), can fit the training sets used, so the study sits entirely in the interpolating regime. No numeric accuracies are given for the width/depth sweeps; trends are read from text and captions. Several rows pool two datasets whose outcomes may differ. One could argue the study is only T3/T5 adjacent, but its post-threshold results bear directly on V1's second descent.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not sweep from underparameterized through the just-fit threshold, establish a peak there, or test a fall-rise-fall curve over a full model-size range. It studies width and depth separately in overparameterized settings.
No epoch-wise fall-rise-fall test-error result is reported.
No test of increased sample size raising test error near an interpolation threshold.
No general double-descent curve across model classes around an interpolation point.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak location across axes.
The study does not test label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or disappearance of a peak under tuned regularization.
The study compares normalization measures for margins, but does not test whether effective parameter counting turns a second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Width and depth sweeps in the tested overparameterized MNIST and CIFAR10 settings
reader_labels.reason: Increasing width improves SGD test accuracy while G&C is mostly stable; increasing depth instead worsens G&C and may worsen or leave SGD unchanged. These results make the generalization trend depend on how overparameterization is increased, but do not test the predicted peak at the interpolation threshold (R1-R14).
